study type: Natural Experimental Study using interrupted time series and difference-in-differences analysis
exposure: Clinical Commissioning Group policies introduced before June 2018 to alter access to knee replacement for patients who were overweight or obese
outcome: rate per 100,000 of primary knee replacement surgery
patient demographics (body mass index, Index of Multiple Deprivation, independently-funded surgery)
cohort: The study included 481,555 patients who had primary knee replacement surgery in England between January 2009 and December 2019.
finding: Rates of primary knee replacement surgery had a sustained fall after the introduction of policies restricting access for overweight or obese patients, while rates increased in localities without such policies.
